sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for the applicant and learned A.G.A. for the State.
This is second bail application.
First bail application has been rejected by Hon'ble Dinesh Kumar Singh, J. for want of prosecution.

Presently, the Hon'ble Judge, who has rejected the first bail application is not sitting at Lucknow, therefore, in view of the administrative order of Acting Chief Justice this second bail application has been put up before the regular Court.

It has been contended by the learned counsel for the applicant that the applicant is in jail since 9.11.2020 in Case Crime No. 434 of 2020 u/s 498A, 304B, 201 IPC & 3/4 Dowry Prohibition Act,
P.S. Phoolbehar, District Lakhimpur Kheri.
It has been submitted that the applicant has been falsely implicated in this case as he has not committed any offence as alleged.
The impugned F.I.R. has been lodged pursuant to the application being filed u/s 156(3) Cr.P.C. for the alleged incident dated 11.1.2019 and the F.I.R. has been lodged on 9.11.2020.

Learned counsel has further submitted that after the death of the wife of the present applicant family members of Balram vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home , ... on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/77741022/

sentences.text: both the sides have entered into compromise in presence of several villagers and due to such compromise neither the inquest report was prepared nor the postmortem was done.

Attention has been drawn towards Annexure no. 4 which is an evidence of complainant / informant / P.W.-1 recorded before the learned court-below on 8.12.2021 wherein while recording his chief-examination and cross-examination he has denied the prosecution story.
He has categorically stated that his daughter was severely ill from the date of her marriage.
She was not able to eat food properly on account of serious ailment in her mouth, therefore, she was only able to eat rice after one or two days.
When she came to know that there is no treatment of her ailment she became frustrated and depressed and on account of such depression she committed suicide.
During cross-examination he has stated that he had not recorded any statement u/s 161 Cr.P.C. as has been shown to him and such statement has been written by the Investigating Officer by his own.
He has also stated in his cross-examination that the in-laws of his daughter were getting her treated and they were trying their level best so that she could recover.

Further attention has been drawn towards Annexure no. 9 and 10 which is the bail orders of the parents of the present applicant namely, Shri Kishan and Smt. Kaushalya who have been granted bail by this Court.
Trial is going on in this case.

The learned counsel for the applicant has given an undertaking on behalf of applicant that the applicant shall not misuse the liberty of bail and shall cooperate with the trial proceedings and shall abide by all terms and conditions of bail, if granted.

Learned A.G.A. opposed the prayer for bail and stated that the present applicant being a husband of the victim, therefore, he may not be absolved from the allegations only on the basis of allegation of the complainant / informant, therefore, his bail application may be rejected.

Without entering into the merits of the case and considering the arguments of learned counsel for the parties, contents and allegations of the F.I.R., the fact that the chief-examination and cross-examination of the informant before the learned trial court wherein he has not supported the prosecution version rather has stated that the present applicant and his family members have not tortured her but his daughter has committed suicide on account of her prolong ailment, trial is going on and the undertaking given on behalf of the applicant that he shall not misuse the liberty of bail and shall cooperate in the trial proceedings, the applicant is entitled to be released on bail in this case.
Let the applicant Balram, involved in aforesaid case crime be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions which are being imposed in the interest of justice:-
(i) The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he shall not seek any adjournment on the dates fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in court.
In case of default of this condition, it shall be open for the trial court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law.

2 (ii) The applicant shall remain present before the trial court on each date fixed, either personally or through his counsel.

sentences.text: In case of his absence, without sufficient cause, the trial court may proceed against him under Section 229-A of the Indian Penal Code.

(iii) In case, the applicant misuses the liberty of bail during trial and in order to secure his presence proclamation under Section 82 Cr.P.C. is issued and the applicant fails to appear before the court on the date fixed in such proclamation,
then, the trial court shall initiate proceedings against him, in accordance with law,
under Section 174-A of the Indian Penal Code.

(iv) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the trial court on the dates fixed for (i) opening of the case, (ii) framing of charge and (iii) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.

If in the opinion of the trial court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the trial court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.
(v) The applicant shall not leave the country without permission of the Court concerned.
Before parting with it is expected that the trial shall be concluded with expedition.
Further, the learned trial court may take all coercive measures as per law if either of the parties do not co-operate in the trial properly.

The learned trial court shall fix short dates to ensure that trial is concluded at the earliest.
.
(Rajesh Singh Chauhan, J.) Order Date :- 15.2.2023
